newsitem.title: INDIA: India's central bank knocks rupee to one-month low.
newsitem.headline: India's central bank knocks rupee to one-month low.

text.p: India's central bank rode a wave of changing sentiment towards the rupee on Friday, buying dollars in the open market to knock the currency to one-month lows.

Traders said the rupee dropped briefly below 35.82 to the dollar after heavy intervention by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) combined with import-related dollar buying and covering of short positions in the interbank market.
By the close of business it was at 35.78/79 against the dollar after starting at 35.705/710.

"It's a combination of factors...RBI buying, import covering, some interbank short-covering," one dealer at a foreign bank in Bombay. "It looks like sentiment has changed, we saw some import covering today for the near months after quite some time."
The RBI, unlike beleaguered central banks in Southeast Asia, has been struggling for the past year with a strong local currency due to heavy inflows of foreign funds and weak import demand.
In the past 12 months it has appreciated by around seven percent.

In recent days the central bank had successfully capped the rupee at 35.70 per dollar, dipping into the market openly or -- to keep the traders guessing -- simply buying the U.S. currency from banks whenever they offered them for sale.
India's authorities are worried that persistent rupee strength could dent exports, which tend to be price-sensitive.
The Commerce Ministry reported on Friday that exports fell 0.95 percent in the first quarter of the financial year beginning April from the same period a year earlier.
Analysts said the drop could be linked to depressed global markets and infrastructure bottlenecks which hold up industrial growth shared the blame along with the rising rupee.

"With the appreciation of the rupee and depreciation of the currency in the surrounding countries there will be some anxieties among the exporters," said V. Raghuraman, Secretary General of the Associated Chambers of Commerce.
